title: Files, Paths and Processes
summary: Working with the operating system - std::fs for reading, writing and listing files, BufReader for large files, Path and PathBuf, io::Error and its kinds, environment variables and arguments, running other programs with std::process::Command, and exit codes.

cards.q: When should you use a `BufReader` instead of `read_to_string`?
cards.a:
When the file may be large, so it is read a piece at a time

`read_to_string` loads the whole file into memory; `BufReader` with `lines()` keeps only a little of it at once. Binary data is what `fs::read` is for.

cards.q: Why pass the arguments to `Command` as a list?
cards.a:
Each argument stays one argument, whatever characters it contains

Nothing is interpreted by a shell, so a file name with spaces or quotes cannot split into several arguments or break the command.

Some("txt")

extension gives the part after the last dot, without the dot, as an Option.
